experiment: Hard-scratchpad follow-up controls: no bridge supervision and parameter-matched dense model
notes: Both controls use the same graph, seed, optimizer and scratchpad depths as the supervised hard-overwrite seed-0 reference.
Held-out facts are learned individually but excluded from all training chains.
Headline evaluation uses two outer steps, each applying the shared block twice.
Two-call depth 1 has the same total block applications as headline native chaining; depth 2 gives each one-hop call the full headline depth.
Native accuracy conditional on both facts being known is informative; two-call accuracy on that same subset is 100% by construction.
Oracle interventions use true intermediate answers at evaluation only and are not ordinary model accuracy.
The dense model fails on trained chains too, so this run does not isolate a generalization disadvantage or establish that dense models cannot compose facts.
One training seed on one graph; no replicated dense-control result or independently tuned dense optimizer.
The no-bridge result establishes failure under this recipe and budget, not a fundamental need for intermediate supervision.
The dense run experienced a laptop sleep interruption; elapsed time is not a controlled speed comparison.
This is the final 2,000-question-per-split GPU evaluation, superseding the earlier 256-question CPU diagnostic.
Checkpoints and datasets remain local under ignored runs/ and data/.
